text:
anika: heads-up — noticed ~10% p99 regression on streamed responses after we enabled continuous-batching v2 with kernel-steer. Seen across smallkernel and largekernel profiles. stack: host10, model: redwood-13b-q4. Link to trace: https://perf.internal/traces/abc123
perfbot: perf alert: p99_lat_streamed +9.8% (24h) — regression window 2004505000-2004506700 :warning:
kevin: thanks. can you paste the profiler flame? also is this KV warmup related?
santiago: saw the same in canary. hypothesis: early flush cadence is preempting partial-decode scheduling and forcing kernel switches mid-batch, leaving batches with mixed kernel hints.
anika: here's a short snippet from the pprof dump:
```text
CPU: 80%
kernel_switch_wait 30%
batching_hold 18%
partial_decode_preempt 12%
kv_cache_miss 8%
other 12%
```
ashley: interesting — kernel selection/switch adds ~1.2-1.6ms per-request when binaries/layout differ. If a micro-batch mixes layouts we pay switch penalty per micro-batch + tail latency.
kevin: quick mitigation idea: when continuous-batching + streaming, prefer stable-kernel grouping — delay admits that would cause a kernel change by a small token_budget window. q-policy: prefer_group_by_kernel affinity.
santiago: can we make that a heuristic toggle? e.g. `prefer_kernel_affinity=true` in batcher config. I tried token_budget_ms=16 on a 12-host canary: p99 -6% but throughput -1.2%. Sounds promising.
anika: canary numbers (12 hosts): baseline p99 72ms -> 64ms with affinity, avg latency stable, tokens/sec -1.2%. KV miss rate unchanged.
kevin: another angle: KV cache warmup — short streamed sessions often have shallow KV population and then get preempted by kernel switch, causing repeated small decodes. Proposal: extend kv_prefetch_window for streaming sessions where continuation_hint=true.
ashley: posted a tiny patch to branch:
```diff
+ preferKernelAffinity bool // defaults false
+ tokenBudgetMs int // used only for streaming admits
```
I'll roll to canary in the morning.
perfbot: rollout status: canary (12 hosts) applied at 2004506900, perf alert cleared in 20m, no downstream regressions flagged.
kevin: next actions: 1) A/B token_budget_ms values (8/16/32) for p99 vs throughput, 2) add kernel-switch-count metric (per-batch), 3) trace-level flag to capture partial-decode preemptions.
anika: I'll open the RFC and a dashboard for kernel-switch-count + per-route token_budget tag. tagging @santiago @ashley for follow-up. :thumbsup:
santiago: acked, will instrument kernel-switch-count and add trace annotation for 'kernel_hint' on micro-batches.
ashley: I also added a short smoke test to ensure streaming + affinity doesn't regress cold-start throughput.
kevin: if canary stays green let's flip the heuristic behind a runtime flag first, then consider default-on for regions with mixed-model workloads.
anika: thanks all — nice debug loop. follow-up in #eng-runtime tomorrow for rollout plan. :rocket:
